reviews.text: Nonetheless, in spite of its very lengthy running time, it feels strangely insubstantial.
reviews.author: Geoffrey Macnab

reviews.text: Eternals feels the most disconnected from previous MCU films, something that is both a blessing and a curse.
reviews.author: Calum Cooper

reviews.text: Watching “Eternals,” it becomes evident that Zhao, the film’s co-writers, and its co-editors wanted emotion to drive the story from its first frame to its last.
reviews.author: Ankit Ojha

reviews.text: It’s not the definitive statement of a brave new world that Marvel probably wanted. But it is a sign at a crossroads, pointing in the right direction.
reviews.author: Joonatan Itkonen

reviews.text: Dear MCU, stop introducing me to a group, and before I have had a chance to warm up to them, break them up and bring them together again.
reviews.author: Sarah Vincent

reviews.text: Chloé Zhao is an incredibly talented filmmaker who is responsible for some of the best films of the last decade. Eternals is sadly not one of them.
reviews.author: Cory Woodroof

reviews.text: Eternals the movie suffers from the same thing The Eternals comic did — it focuses more on a concept than it does on characters.
reviews.author: Jackson Weaver

reviews.text: The Eternals is a jumbled mess because it has to include the origin story plus detail the long lives of the 10 major characters.
reviews.author: Rick Bentley

reviews.text: Chloé Zhao‘s Eternals is Marvel’s most philosophical film to date, teaching us about evolution, humanity, love, and the nature of good and evil.
reviews.author: Serena Seghedoni

reviews.text: Chloe Zhao’s Eternals   is a triumphant! A slow burning story that was epic in nature, beautiful in character development, & Brutal when in its action scenes. So many thoughts, so much ambition, but truly something that the MCU hasn’t seen yet.
reviews.author: Zach Pope

reviews.text: Eternals has its moments but its massive scale never allows the characters to live in their world.
reviews.author: Jillian Chilingerian

reviews.text: Chloé Zhao still follows some of Marvel's success formulas, but her unique style brings new attributes to the cinematic universe, such as the distinctly gorgeous cinematography and the profound themes of faith and humanity.
reviews.author: Manuel São Bento

reviews.text: There are plenty of good ideas here, singular moments to love and appreciate. But at the end of the day, the writing for Eternals trips itself up.
reviews.author: Emma-Jane Betts

reviews.text: Ultimately, Eternals is a superhero movie for people who don’t like the usual superhero fare. It’s far more concerned with grand emotions and the thin line between hero and god than it is with quippy one-liners and over-the-top action.
reviews.author: Tina Kakadelis

reviews.text: As a whole, it’s somewhere in the middle; and I hope it’s not the last time Marvel allows a prestigious director to take a shot in the MCU and give a bold take on the formula, flaws and all.
reviews.author: Benjamin Wiebe

reviews.text: We've seen lots of heroes fight for revenge, duty, honor, glory or adventure, but rarely love which is a prime motivating force for all of us.
reviews.author: Joseph Garcia

reviews.text: The narrative is simultaneously too large and too small. With personal relationships defining the narrative of a cosmos spanning opera ... As far as MCU goes though this isn't a terrible direction for them to explore.
reviews.author: Taylor Baker

reviews.text: [Chloé Zhao’s] Marvel debut is the opposite of anything she’s ever done — she has created something stale, repetitious, and heavy-handed. I’m sorry to say Eternals is a massive disappointment.
reviews.author: M.N. Miller

reviews.text: The result is a beautiful look into the joys and sorrows of humanity that also doubles as an entry point into some of Marvel’s stranger cosmic storytelling.
reviews.author: Breeze Riley

reviews.text: I couldn’t help but think of how it would have fared better as a Disney+ streaming series. There’s very little here that screams big screen movie, and giving the characters and their stories more room to develop would have helped tremendously.
reviews.author: Keith Garlington

reviews.text: Eternals is a jam-packed, ambitious and oddly imperfect addition to the Marvelverse.
reviews.author: Cris Kennedy

reviews.text: Eternals may be one of the weakest Marvel movies yet, but there is still enough to enjoy as it propels us into a new and uncertain future for the franchise.
reviews.author: Daniel Howat

reviews.text: Chloé Zhao tries to shove a sappy essay on the virtues of mankind and the value of loving humanity despite its flaws into a lackluster superhero journey of ten vapid characters who spend the entire film disproving her theory.
reviews.author: Alachia Queen

reviews.text: ETERNALS is love! Chloé Zhao has created such a beautiful film. Her superheroes are awe-inspiring supernatural beings and at the same time so deeply human.
reviews.author: Jimmy Cage

reviews.text: We have to wonder what kind of movie Zhao would have made left to her own devices. We suspect it would have less CGI monsters and more ruminations on character, immortality and watching humanity evolve.
reviews.author: David Reddish

reviews.text: Its a beautiful film to watch with visually stunning sequences worthy of the big screen experience.
reviews.author: Thomas Stoneham-Judge

reviews.text: A film that takes an age to arrive at a familiar place. Yes, there are a plethora of new terms, species, and legends to learn, but it all boils down to heroes preparing for the big battle at the end. Its visually impressive, but missing the sense of fun.
reviews.author: Victoria Luxford

reviews.text: An interesting storyline in the Marvel Universe that in my opinion, proves how the status quo just might miss the most impactful reason comic books existed in the first place. In my view, comic readers will likely appreciate this movie more.
reviews.author: Vincent Schilling

reviews.text: Hampered by too many characters, the plot is equally underdeveloped beyond the major beats.
reviews.author: Marya E. Gates

reviews.text: "The harder this intermediary, conceptually fascinating Marvel chapter veers from the familiar, the harder it collides with the guardrails of frustrating MCU formula."
reviews.author: David Lynch

reviews.text: Mind you, it is one of the weaker MCU outings, but is it really inferior to some of the Iron Man and Thor entries?
reviews.author: Matt Brunson

reviews.text: Writer and director Chlo Zhao, who won an Oscar for Nomadland, has given audiences a plodding, nonsensical film bereft of feeling and action.
reviews.author: Collin Garbarino

reviews.text: Zhao ultimately robs the artist’s comic of its sweep by constantly turning a space opera into a repetitive character drama.
reviews.author: Ed Gonzalez

reviews.text: Eternals is driven by a love story. One between lovers, duty, and legacy. Throughout the 157-minute runtime, viewers will have their eyes glued to the screen and rediscover what it means to be excited about something original.
reviews.author: Josie Meléndez

reviews.text: Marvel Studios' Eternals is a rare misfire. However, it has a few redeeming qualities. Chloe Zhao had some clear ambition, but the film fails to come together with likable, meaningful characters or a truly engaging plot
reviews.author: Jeffrey Harris

reviews.text: With Eternals, Disney seems to have settled on a galaxy-spanning villain that could hang over the entirety of their Phase IV efforts, but the film might just feel too obvious to entice the legion of franchise fans to their latest lengthy story arc.
reviews.author: Wesley Lovell

reviews.text: Eternals is as good as it could have been. The issues stem from the source material and the movie acts as a huge set-up for what's to come.
reviews.author: Jeff Nelson

reviews.text: Eternals is nothing short of a disaster.
reviews.author: Carson Timar

reviews.text: Though there’s definitely some fun to be had with this film beyond Zhao’s glorious compositions, Eternals ends up being one of the more overwrought and, frankly, silly additions to the MCU canon.
reviews.author: Joshua Axelrod

reviews.text: Eternals, which boasts the most diverse Marvel cast to date, may not be to everybody's taste-particularly those who find comfort in tradition.
reviews.author: Mimi Wong

reviews.text: Eternals is a really hard one to rate. Thinking about it although I enjoyed a lot more of it than I didn't I don't know if I'll ever feel like watching it again...
reviews.author: David Hogan

reviews.text: Eternals is overly ambitious in some areas, but it has plenty left to explore and improve going forward.
reviews.author: Jordy Sirkin

reviews.text: In two and a half rather long hours, the only thing I find is a boredom as infinite as the universe with the politically correct origin story of these Marvel's Power Rangers. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Yasser Medina

reviews.text: It's not until the heart of the second act that we're totally immersed in the plot with its twists and the direction it is going to take from there. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Sergio López Aguirre

reviews.text: In the MCU, even the not-great movies are reasonably entertaining, and worth a watch. Eternals is the rare franchise entry that's a major misfire.
reviews.author: John Serba

reviews.text: Eternals is a celebration of humanity, warts and all.
reviews.author: Victor Stiff

reviews.text: The abundance of story, characters, and world-building can be overwhelming, but Zhao approaches it brilliantly. Nanjiani saves this film for me.
reviews.author: Rosa Parra

reviews.text: Eternals is stuck between a rock and a hard place. It is too blatantly commercial to take advantage of the studio's new prestigious filmmaking talent and too outside the box to satisfy Marvel's audience.
reviews.author: Harris Dang

reviews.text: Eternals pushes the envelope both visually and narratively, taking the superhero franchise to new and exciting directions. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Rene Sanchez

reviews.text: It doesn't have one remarkable element, performance, scene, or moment in its two and a half hour running time that made me think I was watching something marvelous.
reviews.author: Dan Buffa

reviews.text: Eternals offers too much interesting stuff to be dismissed as "bad" outright, but it's frustratingly uneven.
reviews.author: Sarah Marrs

reviews.text: In snatches, it gives us a genuine moment of visual specificity that works but it cannot keep up the weight of all the questions and implications that it depends on. If it must be all things to everyone, then it ends up being little unto itself.
reviews.author: Andrew Kendall

reviews.text: Eternals is far from perfect, but it pushes the MCU into promising new territory....it feels like an amalgam of what Marvel does best - splendidly chaotic fight scenes, dazzling special effects, and stories that speak to who we are as human beings.
reviews.author: Michael Blackmon

reviews.text: ...a completely misguided and misbegotten piece of work that stands as the absolute nadir of both the Marvel Cinematic Universe and Zhao's filmography...
reviews.author: David Nusair

reviews.text: But at this point, the MCU formula has been recycled so often that sitting through these movies starts to feel eternal.
reviews.author: Noah Berlatsky

reviews.text: It is an okay movie but the characters didn't grab me and the -lot was too drawn out.
reviews.author: Jackie K. Cooper

reviews.text: Well, they can't all be winners. With the arrival of Chloé Zhao's Eternals, somewhere Alan Taylor, director of Thor: The Dark World, is breathing a sigh of relief; he's no longer responsible for the worst Marvel film.
reviews.author: Travis Johnson

reviews.text: Eternals is a beautifully made, well-acted film with characters I can't wait to see more of.
reviews.author: George Clark

reviews.text: Eternals takes aim at some cool ideas and concepts, and it mostly delivers...
reviews.author: Eric Eisenberg

reviews.text: Zhao is quite literally providing us the best of both worlds as a result. Eternals simultaneously feels like an MCU film and a prestige picture with everything that entails.
reviews.author: Jared Mobarak

reviews.text: A thoughtful and earthy epic that dares to ask big questions and acknowledge its characters' weaknesses.
reviews.author: Mattie Lucas

reviews.text: A philosophically dense film that stagnates under its own considerable weight as it dances through 7000 years of world cultures while never quite finding its groove.
reviews.author: Andrea Chase

reviews.text: "Eternals" isn't a terrible Marvel movie, just an average one. Considering the talent at work, and the potential of such a world-changing set of heroes, it could have been so much more.
reviews.author: Sean P. Means

reviews.text: It's baffling how low-energy Eternals is. It looks like a film made by people who work in an office.
reviews.author: Sean Gilman

reviews.text: Eternals is a slow-paced affair that runs too long and never quite delivers heart-stopping moments.
reviews.author: Mark Meszoros

reviews.text: Eternals makes for an alienating first watch. ... Dig a little deeper, however, and this behemoth of a superhero flick has its rewards too.
reviews.author: Caroline Siede

reviews.text: ... everything fans expect from Marvel Studios while still feeling a bit hollow... fuel for the imagination... angsty and lovelorn but adds few revelations to the who-wants-to-live-forever trope...
reviews.author: Kevin A. Ranson

reviews.text: This movie needed better marketing as it was an epic drama with superheroes in it. The comic relief was very much needed because this was a pretty slow movie.
reviews.author: Justin Brown

reviews.text: There a solid performances, beautiful cinematography and decent story that was better than I expected. However this film felt and was incredibly long...
reviews.author: Brandon Collins

reviews.text: It comes with all the childish nonsense over superheroes you get from juvenile comic books.
reviews.author: Dennis Schwartz

reviews.text: Academy Award Winner Chloe Zhao's "Eternals" is not good, but unlike the slew of increasingly tiring and formulaic Marvel fare there are some bright spots.
reviews.author: Blake Howard

reviews.text: Without a strong human-level side to balance it all out, big concepts are just lifeless words and images.
reviews.author: Anthony Morris

reviews.text: Tedious. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Marcelo Stiletano

reviews.text: Eternals is just as ambitious and argumentatively dispersed as the original comic series. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Fausto Fernandez

reviews.text: Good without being great, Eternals is an enjoyable but bloated push into Marvel's cosmic comics catalogue.
reviews.author: Matt Neal

reviews.text: An epic that feels far smaller than it should.
reviews.author: Rob Hunter

reviews.text: Chloe Zhao has made a flawed film, it's true, though it's bursting with beauty and ambition. It's possible this might be the best-looking film in the MCU, and Zhao gifts us with strong cinematography and numerous shots of gorgeous vistas.
reviews.author: Tim Brennan

reviews.text: A more than two and a half hour pompous and leaden film. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Javier Ocaña

reviews.text: Zhao brings her flair for the beauty of the eye shots over vast landscapes...and it still delivers on the celestial plains of epic proportions. It's a cosmic opening for the next phase of the Marvel saga.
reviews.author: Zehra Phelan

reviews.text: It's a frustrating, occasionally fun, at points brilliant, frequently tiresome journey that never manages to reach any of the potential it so clearly had.
reviews.author: Rhys Bowen Jones

reviews.text: This one captured my eye as well as my intrigue for this continuing storyline in ways I had not anticipated
reviews.author: Steven Prokopy

reviews.text: Introducing a dozen characters and establishing their backstories in an already busy plot is a heavy lift. Director Chloé Zhao (Nomadland) skillfully juggles all these elements, making an understandable 2.5 hour movie that covers all the bases.
reviews.author: Robert Roten

reviews.text: What might have been a fascinating interplay of psychologies and ideas, is rendered in broad, lifeless strokes.
reviews.author: Ed Whitfield

reviews.text: Eternals is somehow Marvel's most ambitious movie and also its worst.
reviews.author: Mike McGranaghan

reviews.text: Eternals is dull, it's boring, and it's quite epically uninvolving.
reviews.author: Paul Mount

reviews.text: Taking up space in such a well-mined universe can't be easy, but Eternals not only manages to hold its own, but delivers something engaging, unique, funny and warm.
reviews.author: Gemma Creagh

reviews.text: The one exception to the film's utterly bloodless chemistry is a cameo by a post-credits pop star who, for all of 15 seconds, has a completely charming interaction with a CG creature. I believed that performance more than anything in the 2.5 hours.
reviews.author: Matt Baume

reviews.text: Bring in the portentous overreach of the Eternals' cosmos-shaking storyline, though, and her talent is diminished. For Zhao, bigger is not better.
reviews.author: Alison Gillmor

reviews.text: At its best, this is galaxy-brain, comic-book stuff rooted in a tactile sense of place.
reviews.author: Josh Larsen

reviews.text: Eternals has a lot of heart and beauty that drips off the screen when you watch it.
reviews.author: Amanda Reimer

reviews.text: For a movie with ten protagonists, it's impressive that each character is given a unique personality.
reviews.author: Rachael Harper

reviews.text: Clearly, we're supposed to leave the cinema filled with an urgent sense of anticipation. But all I felt was relief that the two-and-a-half hour running time had finally come to an end.
reviews.author: Sandra Hall

reviews.text: Chloe Zhao maintains a terrific spark in the character interaction, and the plot has some thrilling twists and turns.
reviews.author: Rich Cline

reviews.text: Chloé Zhao's take on the Marvel Universe is a far cry from her last film, Nomadland. While Eternals has its moments, it is not one of the Marvel greats.
reviews.author: Aine O'Connor

reviews.text: The enthralling action set-pieces have to be parsed from in-between awkward moments in which characters stand around waiting to explain themselves. The wildly inconsistent tone moves from laugh-out-loud to deadly earnest...
reviews.author: Nandini Ramnath

reviews.text: Eternals represents the kind of grand, open-hearted home run swings that Hollywood should be more willing to embrace.
reviews.author: Matt Conway

reviews.text: Those who have followed Zhao's meditative, self-reflective work will know that her language of communication is a blend of deep silences and aching words.
reviews.author: Renuka Vyavahare

reviews.text: Despite being 2 hours 37 minutes long, Eternals feels rushed, like it's trying to squeeze a ten-episode series into one feature film.
reviews.author: George Wu

reviews.text: Zhao's approach can feel like a director at war with the very nature of the material she has been hired to direct.... Eternals can still be admired for its chutzpah.
reviews.author: Alci Rengifo

reviews.text: An ambitious mess and a fascinating failure
reviews.author: Jeffrey Zhang

reviews.text: It mixes melancholy with violence and humour, styles clashing, the artsy vs. the "Marvel way," with cartoonish digital creations and all. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Sebastian Zavala Kahn

reviews.text: Eternals isn't a complete success, with issues large and small. That said...it's an impressive effort. This is a BIG swing, and while it might not be a home run, we're looking at some solid contact. For an undertaking like this, that's a win.
reviews.author: Allen Adams

reviews.text: A slack film, in the way one gets to be when one has no pressing need to come in at a reasonable running time.
reviews.author: Tim Brayton

reviews.text: The long and short of it is that, yes, Eternals is a colossal bore...for those lacking patience, heart, and imagination.
reviews.author: Ian Simmons

reviews.text: On the whole, the film succeeds in becoming the series' most emotional outing.
reviews.author: Hanna Flint

reviews.text: Eternals creates the illusion of a maturity that would have elevated it to director Chloé Zhao's standards. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Orlando Maldonado

reviews.text: None of the characters come across and compelling...yes, these being are supposed to be immortal, but you'll feel as if you're time with the Eternals has lasted for an eternity.
reviews.author: Michael Medved

reviews.text: Chloé Zhao deals with real world themes that resonate now and will only resonate more as the MCU continues to evolve.
reviews.author: Kent Garrison

reviews.text: Eternals is not a good movie. It's not a good comic book movie, it's not a good action movie, it's not a good Marvel movie. It somehow feels overstuffed and empty at the same time. It's muddled and convoluted. It's a bland and boring and bewildering mess.
reviews.author: Robert Slack

reviews.text: Eternals is a mess, a beautiful mess, but a mess nonetheless. There is a far more interesting movie under all that flotsam. In better hands, the movie could have been something special. All Zhao has provided is a bland, dull film.
reviews.author: Kshitij Rawat

reviews.text: I came out disappointed having witnessed an imbalanced, slightly messy, uninspiring, and sadly boring slog.
reviews.author: Matt Hudson

reviews.text: For all its flaws, it is far from the worst entry in the MCU, but it is, perhaps, the first of Marvel's films to be less than the sum of its parts.
reviews.author: Christopher Machell

reviews.text: In many ways, what it means to be human is the central question that drives Eternals... But the movie's dizzying star power and twisty backstories render it too clunky and overstuffed to concisely answer said central question.
reviews.author: Kylie Cheung

reviews.text: I really enjoyed Eternals despite it being too long, and one of the reasons was the humor. Another was just that it felt kind of quirky and different from most Marvel movies these days.
reviews.author: Erik Kain

reviews.text: An exciting peek into the future of the franchise....with grander ideas and new types of storytelling.
reviews.author: Karen M. Peterson

reviews.text: Marvel is the peanut butter of movies, Zhao is the filet mignon of directors, and I just wasn't fully enjoying my peanut butter steak.
reviews.author: Aaron Dicer

reviews.text: It's not that none of the movie works. It's that none of it works for very long.
reviews.author: Nathaniel Rogers

reviews.text: The MCU's first DCEU film.
reviews.author: Edwin Arnaudin

reviews.text: Gorgeous and vacant, The Eternals is the most numbing entry in Marvel's 13-year-old MCU franchise -- even as it struggles to be its weirdest and most philosophical.
reviews.author: John Wenzel

reviews.text: Exciting, yet exhausting introduction to a new set of Marvel superheroes with an emphasis on eclectic diversity and familial inclusion.
reviews.author: Susan Granger

reviews.text: Eternals is not perfect for the stumbling beginning and Jolie plays a character that doesn't seem fully fleshed out on screen. She doesn't quite fit in. But overall, it's one of the best MCU experiences for it's eccentric and endearing characters.
reviews.author: Lee McCoy

reviews.text: Eternals is a flawed experiment years ahead of its industry but, sooner or later, a film has to break the mold and prove superheroes are worthy of deeper, richer cinematic retellings.
reviews.author: Alicia Gilstorf

reviews.text: While it has big special effects scenes, it's not a formulaic Marvel film. While there are certainly typical action scenes, the movie digs deeper into the dynamic of multiple layers of relationships and dark human drama.
reviews.author: Nathalia Aryani

reviews.text: Eternals offers plenty to embrace...the overall production is just not effective enough to move into the upper echelon of Marvel films.
reviews.author: Michael Ward

reviews.text: [Director Chloé Zhao] is in the mouth of the Marvel beast with this one. It can devour even the most able-eyed filmmaker, which is exactly what Eternals does.
reviews.author: Candice McMillan

reviews.text: For all the effort that has gone into ensuring representation in the casting, the storytelling, with its forced flashbacks and synthetic sentiment, lets the whole thing down.
reviews.author: Wendy Ide

reviews.text: But like Galactus gobbling a planet, Zhao's unique filmmaking style has been subsumed by the mighty Marvel maw
reviews.author: Eli Glasner

reviews.text: With 10 superheroes to introduce and millennia of backstories to plough through, this 157-minute slog requires superhuman levels of endurance.
reviews.author: Andy Lea

reviews.text: The MCU reaches a theatrical low point with "Eternals," an odd team-up adventure that teases a franchise the future of which might be better suited for Disney's streaming service.
reviews.author: Jonathan W. Hickman

reviews.text: Even acclaimed filmmaker Chloe Zhao, who collected Best Picture and Director Oscars for last year's 'Nomadland,' can't save her first venture into the MC Universe from being laughable too often in all the wrong places.
reviews.author: John Urbancich

reviews.text: Regardless of Zhao's (and Marvel's) intentions, "Eternals" is a parade of faces without experience, a movie that reaches back and forth through history and comes back empty-handed.
reviews.author: Richard Brody

reviews.text: Trying to save the world shouldn't be boring, but Eternals is one big giant yawn - and easily the worst film in the Marvel Cinematic Universe.
reviews.author: Lynn Venhaus

reviews.text: A beautiful new entry in the MCU
reviews.author: Kathia Woods

reviews.text: Chloe Zhao is a very talented director, but perhaps it was too much to expect her go from the sparse, quiet life of Nomadland to this special effects driven action blockbuster with a huge cast of characters who are not very exciting.
reviews.author: Linda and Al Lerner

reviews.text: While it delivers the action and eye candy, "Eternals" is middling Marvel.
reviews.author: Russ Simmons

reviews.text: This is one of the more forgettable MCU movies, despite the direction of Oscar winner Chloé Zhao.
reviews.author: Richard Roeper

reviews.text: Where should we start-the bored facial expressions, the flaccid cinematography, or the complete lack of chemistry between two insanely hot people?
reviews.author: Laura Bradley

reviews.text: I wish somebody would give a map to exit the Marvel Universe at some point. I felt like I was lost in a made up world I did not particularly care about.
reviews.author: Andy Klein

reviews.text: Eternals seems to exist in the bizarre liminal space between expectations and indifference.
reviews.author: Kevin Fallon

reviews.text: At a glacial pace of 2 hours and 37 minutes, the movie occasionally feels eternal, and it sags under that weight.
reviews.author: Claudia Puig

reviews.text: I certainly can't get emotionally invested anymore...it's just a series of special effects interspersed with a bit of humor...
reviews.author: Mark Kermode

reviews.text: The entire movie felt like an overlong parody...
reviews.author: Shawn Edwards

reviews.text: Externals wobbles under an expository burden that operates like tow ropes on a fractured narrative.
reviews.author: Robert Denerstein

reviews.text: It's enjoyable, and it's funny, and its actors truly are terrific. Perhaps it's too much of what it doesn't need, and not enough of what it does. Or maybe it's something simpler - maybe it's that Marvel's reach finally exceeded its grasp.
reviews.author: TK Burton

reviews.text: Chloé Zhao... manages to deliver on every front when it comes to this movie.
reviews.author: Aiko Hilkinger

reviews.text: [Chloe Zhao] puts into full view the kind of moral quandaries that Marvel's only ever really danced around in the past... But there's only so much room for that kind of thought.
reviews.author: Clarisse Loughrey

reviews.text: You can absolutely believe that this is a Marvel movie made by the director of Nomadland.
reviews.author: Kevin Carr

reviews.text: It's a brave thing to take the series into mystical territory, and I can't help but admire how elastic the Marvel formula has proved.
reviews.author: Kristian M. Lin

reviews.text: Zhao's deep sense of the rhythms that pass unspoken between people... are exactly what makes Eternals such a memorable, unfamiliar and refreshing film to watch.
reviews.author: Graeme Tuckett

reviews.text: Unfortunately, the film's strict adherence to the Marvel formula keeps the whole enterprise from really working.
reviews.author: Abby Olcese

reviews.text: Chloe Zhao takes a huge swing here to shake it up for Marvel, and that's worth applauding.
reviews.author: Paul McGuire Grimes

reviews.text: Eternals tries to work with a lot of moving parts and takes some really big swings. Sometimes it hits, and sometimes it doesn't. For that reason, Eternals and Chloé Zhao deserve credit for giving the MCU something more original.
reviews.author: Emmanuel Noisette

reviews.text: Eternals is, to put it mildly, a vast undertaking in the storytelling department. This creates both pluses and minuses for the film.
reviews.author: Damond Fudge

reviews.text: Eternalsis a good film...not great...and presents a different slice of the enormous MCU pie.
reviews.author: Alan Ng

reviews.text: If you're not put off by the ponderous pacing or the humble lack of gaudy flair, this film offers not only an evolution of the comic book film genre but also a revolution in representation.
reviews.author: Jon Espino

reviews.text: Eternals is an uncharacteristically sloppy misfire.
reviews.author: Jeva Lange

reviews.text: Like an X-Men movie if all the characters were Cyclops.
reviews.author: Doug Walker

reviews.text: You have to commend the effort to take the MCU in a different direction, but there's little else worthy of applause.
reviews.author: Olly Richards

reviews.text: Chloé Zhao's dreadfully dull Marvel movie "Eternals" should really have been titled "Loiterers."
reviews.author: Peter Howell

reviews.text: Never have the stakes been higher or as instantly forgettable in a Marvel movie as this.
reviews.author: Stephen Garrett

reviews.text: Running almost long enough for a pair of films, Zhao flits between her characters and only occasionally gives them room to shine. If she cut her team down to the size of a basketball squad, there would be more room for chemistry and character development.
reviews.author: Dan Lybarger

reviews.text: All of the effects-driven spectacle serves a silly and overwrought story that leaves little room for meaningful character development or emotional depth.
reviews.author: Todd Jorgenson

reviews.text: I don't think Zhao should be chided for attempting a film so seemingly outside her comfort zone. No director should have to commit to a career of specialization. The only qualm I have about Eternals is that it's not better.
reviews.author: Peter Rainer

reviews.text: By the tale's end, it becomes clear that Eternals' true aspiration is to be an arthouse blockbuster in much the same vein as the works of Denis Villeneuve and The Wachowskis.
reviews.author: Jennifer Heaton

reviews.text: An amazingly talented cast - playing surprisingly nuanced characters - is forced to dial every performance to "I can't believe Tide got the stain out!" levels. It's Shakespeare by Cliff's Notes, a Kidz Bop Nirvana cover, a musical episode of The Wire.
reviews.author: Ryan Syrek

reviews.text: Eternals is a frustratingly dense and heinously overcomplicated film that loses Zhao's delicate filmmaking sensibilities in its rush to introduce swathes of new Marvel heroes.
reviews.author: Lauren Coates

reviews.text: If a movie is as good as its characters, then 'Eternals' is still a good movie, one that I've been enjoying thinking about again and again.
reviews.author: Jeffrey M. Anderson

reviews.text: Chloe Zhao has succumbed to corporate filmmaking anonymity.
reviews.author: James Verniere

reviews.text: Because there's so many characters to meet (all well-developed and unique), the structure of the narrative struggles with momentum.
reviews.author: Jason Escamilla

reviews.text: The use of tendrils of light connecting the superheroes is impressive and the special effects at the end are truly mind-blowing, but the film is mostly saved by Nanjiani, whose humor and delivery makes him seem like he's in another movie.
reviews.author: Mark Kennedy

reviews.text: A powerful, sweeping exploration of love, life, and the MCU's history, Eternals occasionally stumbles, but when it soars, this is Marvel Studios at its magnificent best.
reviews.author: Josh Wilding

reviews.text: I admire the ambition. I worry that Marvel will take away the message not to take any more chances and return to formula. That's not the right decision.
reviews.author: Dan Murrell

reviews.text: It's both nowhere near as bad as the Rotten Tomatoes discourse would have you believe and also nowhere near as exemplary as the rabid fan base's dogmatic defenses online may have warranted.
reviews.author: Dominic Griffin

reviews.text: Diversity & fluidity is a plus, but Chloe Zhao's influence is absent in this team forms-breaks up-reforms retread, & it unfolds slower than an 8-room canvas tent. Bollywood!
reviews.author: Patrick McDonald

reviews.text: Too many C-team superheroes...
reviews.author: Kurt Loder

reviews.text: There is plenty to criticize in Eternals-and some things that I might praise, in another story set in another universe-but I'm not sure any story set in this universe could possibly offer anything to care about one way or the other.
reviews.author: Steven D. Greydanus

reviews.text: It's not as bad or as disappointing as some critics and fanboys/girls might lead you to believe, but it can't shake that "been there, seen that before" aura.
reviews.author: Jim Judy

reviews.text: As big as things are in the film, the stakes have never felt any smaller.
reviews.author: Matt Rodriguez

reviews.text: Little is at stake, and there is a tenuous - at best - connection with the rest of the Marvel heroes and villains.
reviews.author: Phil Villarreal

reviews.text: Only the gift of eternal life will stop you looking at your watch, willing the final credits to hove in to sight.
reviews.author: Brian Viner

reviews.text: If they weren't dressed like members of Earth Wind & Fire you could be forgiven for thinking you were watching a left-wing book group in a trendier corner of Portland
reviews.author: Donald Clarke

reviews.text: Although it's ultimately enjoyable, a film this epic shouldn't feel like just another step in the MCU timeline.
reviews.author: Johnny Gayzmonic

reviews.text: Eternals sags under many conflicting demands that the film attempts to cater to.
reviews.author: Anupama Chopra

reviews.text: Marvel's first DC movie.
reviews.author: Sonny Bunch

reviews.text: All superhero movies are ridiculous. That's where the super part comes in. With the good superhero movies, you don't notice the ridiculousness - or it doesn't matter. With "Eternals," you notice.
reviews.author: Mark Feeney

reviews.text: Zhao's "Eternals" offers an alternative approach to the repetitive Marvel movies.
reviews.author: Dustin Chase

reviews.text: With Eternals, Marvel proves itself to be nothing more than a staid, lumbering black hole.
reviews.author: Angelica Jade Bastién

reviews.text: Eternals is two steps forwards for representation but three steps backwards for dramatic ingenuity.
reviews.author: Kevin Maher

reviews.text: ETERNALS is exactly how we can continue to get Marvel movies without the formula feeling stale, while still scratching the itch audiences have for big, bombastic, superpowered action.
reviews.author: Kevin Brackett

reviews.text: Eternals turns into reality what seemed impossible: that a superhero movie, in addition to being boring, can be tremendously pedantic.
reviews.author: Víctor López G.

reviews.text: Eternals is bold, beautiful, and brilliant. Unlike anything the MCU has seen before.
reviews.author: Brandon Avery

reviews.text: Eternals is not a bad movie per-se, just an immensely underwhelming one. These cosmic beings are portrayed as saviors of humanity who care about mere mortals, but the filmmakers seem to forget to give us a reason to care for ANY of them.
reviews.author: Ruth Maramis

reviews.text: An awkward series of murky flashbacks provides a disjointed Eternals origin story while attempting to build to the obligatory Armageddon-like battle at the end.
reviews.author: Lisa Johnson Mandell

reviews.text: Eternals is the least fun I've ever had in a MCU film.
reviews.author: Tom Santilli

reviews.text: Eternals arrives as Marvel's greatest failure and feels like the worst Power Rangers adaptation yet conceived.
reviews.author: Jay Horton

reviews.text: [Director Chloé Zhao does] more than well enough, even though the story, stretched out over 157 minutes, is rambling and repetitive.
reviews.author: Joe Morgenstern

reviews.text: The movie walks away from the formula that Marvel has given us for the last 15 years...and IT'S GOOD.[Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Gabriela Meza

reviews.text: A turn in the Marvel universe where characters, their fears and emotions take center stage which in turn raises the stakes in the action beats and for their arcs in the future. Better than any of the Marvel films released this year.
reviews.author: Erik Childress

reviews.text: Zhao, an arthouse director known for her award-winning dramas that imbue working-class struggles with poetry was hired to add a touch of prestige drama to a comic-book tale. She elevates the material in some places.
reviews.author: John Lui

reviews.text: The depth of character too is slight, and the CGI effects don't really break any ground -- and occasionally look Sharknado cheesy.
reviews.author: Tom Meek

reviews.text: The saddest superhero movie. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Luis Martínez

reviews.text: While sometimes when Marvel gets out of its comfort zone, audiences enjoy gems like Guardians of the Galaxy, this time the results are far less successful and quite frankly disappointing.
reviews.author: Kyle Wilson

reviews.text: Eternals is an unfocused mess of a story that features a wonderfully diverse cast that has no chemistry.
reviews.author: Michelle Kisner

reviews.text: The thought of a total bomb detonating onscreen is a ripe prospect, until a doomed movie demonstrates that it is just bad, as minute by minute, hour by hour, you sit through one like Eternals.
reviews.author: Ray Pride

reviews.text: Time will tell if it pays off and if the various parts easily connect. Not every entry in the earlier series was a success. For those who enjoyed the ride, Eternals is a good start to the adventure ahead.
reviews.author: Daniel M. Kimmel

reviews.text: This film doesn't follow the usual MCU structure, and I, for one, am happy to have something that feels fresh in a movie franchise that's been going on for more than 10 years.
reviews.author: Jamal Grootboom

reviews.text: This is without a doubt the worst MCU film to date and the sort of rancid theater experience that makes you want to rethink the whole thing and burn it to the ground.
reviews.author: Steve Katz

reviews.text: The elements seem to be there for "Eternals" to further stretch the boundaries of what constitutes a Marvel movie but too much of the time, it settles for being more of the same.
reviews.author: Chris Hewitt

reviews.text: It's sprawling and somber, collapsing under the weight of its own misguided ambitions.
reviews.author: Josh Bell

reviews.text: Despite its obvious flaws, it's easy to appreciate the willingness to try something different in Eternals.
reviews.author: George M. Thomas

reviews.text: It's an awkward mix of unconvincing, pinball-machine Marvel action and earnest -- often confused -- sentiment.
reviews.author: Luke Goodsell

reviews.text: At its best, Eternals brims with the sense of possibility that makes comic books, which inspired this mega-blockbuster film franchise, so thrilling and so enduring.
reviews.author: Eric Webb

reviews.text: With beautiful visuals, some of the most innovative action scenes from the studio, and a deep sense of love to the characters and their clash of ideologies, Eternals is so flawed yet so emotionally rich.
reviews.author: Kevin L. Lee

reviews.text: While Eternals has considerable strengths, it is somewhat lacking in ... fun [and] adventurousness.
reviews.author: Sean Collier

reviews.text: Eternals may not be your typical comic book film, but it's a refreshing new vision thanks to Zhao's confident filmmaking.
reviews.author: Micheal Compton

reviews.text: Long, clumsy, and repetitive explanations abound. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Benjamín Harguindey

reviews.text: Pretty images can only go so far and Eternals can't quite rise to its own formidable goals.
reviews.author: Terence Johnson

reviews.text: The flashbacks interrupt whatever momentum Zhao builds, while the yammer only further muddies an already convoluted story.
reviews.author: Manohla Dargis

reviews.text: The glacial pace of the piece makes sense ... given how time must appear to those for whom it never ends. Despite the heavy use of exposition ... nothing else proves as logical.
reviews.author: Christopher Llewellyn Reed

reviews.text: Something as huge in scale and scope on the surface shouldn't seem this dull and perfunctory.
reviews.author: Mark Dujsik

reviews.text: Opts for an emotional, biblical edge that is likely to test the genre puritans who prefer brawl to brains.
reviews.author: Peter Gray

reviews.text: It's not a drastic enough change to freak out the faithful or demolish the formula, but it's a pleasant enough experience, and its aesthetic instinct skews toward the pretty and expansive.
reviews.author: Jason Shawhan

reviews.text: At a run time of two hours and thirty-seven minutes, the movie drags at points and doesn't really seem to be going anywhere very fast.
reviews.author: Allison Rose

reviews.text: There's something uniformly placid about the performances, not helped by the cameo-length appearances by much of the wasted cast...
reviews.author: Richard Whittaker

reviews.text: It's ambitious, but tonal shifts abound and by the time the CGI orgy of the finale gets underway, Eternals simultaneously feels like too much and too little.
reviews.author: Richard Crouse

reviews.text: Zhao unfurls the story of the Eternals on an epic and elaborate stage ... that ends up being a double-edged sword. We get a grandiose mythology ... alongside backstories ... [but] we are never given the time to understand, care for, or connect with them.
reviews.author: Akhil Arora

reviews.text: There are some nice touches and an attractive new diversity worn lightly, but this is an underpowered and uncertain film.
reviews.author: Peter Bradshaw

reviews.text: Eternals, despite trying to be a departure from the superhero generic norm, misses wide of the mark and ends up being a major lapse.
reviews.author: James Berardinelli

reviews.text: While it ultimately gives in to the demands of the MCU,Eternalsstrives to be more than just another superhero movie. It's the reason why it has won me over, and may be the reason why it won't work for others.
reviews.author: Travis Hopson

reviews.text: Call me basic, but I miss the old Marvel. Eternals is not all bad, and will appeal to many. An unnecessary sex scene makes it non-kid-friendly for some families.
reviews.author: Tania Lamb

reviews.text: To sum it up, "The Eternals" - the third film in the Fourth Phase of the MCU -is another fine addition to the series that may itself be eternal.
reviews.author: Michael A. Smith

reviews.text: Sluggishly directed, it's a thunderously dull bland-out stuffed with all the things we've seen quite enough of: fights with big-jawed monsters; eyes that shoot energy beams; self-important longueurs; an all-but-incomprehensible story. Seriously: enough.
reviews.author: Jim Schembri

reviews.text: One of the best things about "Eternals", is how it feels like a superhero movie for everyone. If you have yet to feel seen through a hero, then you might connect with one of these diverse characters.
reviews.author: Susan Kamyab

reviews.text: Eternals is messy but there is beauty in its parts if not necessarily the sum.
reviews.author: Wenlei Ma

reviews.text: Chloé Zhao manages to forge this spectacle about gods and monsters into one of the most human Marvel films to date. Still, the seams of this unwieldy amalgam are showing and stretched.
reviews.author: Neil Morris

reviews.text: The pacing's off, the constant jumping between past and present doesn't help the flow of the story, and none of the set pieces leap off the screen.
reviews.author: Rebecca Murray

reviews.text: Immortal weirdos hash out philosophy amidst an apocalyptic road trip - 'Wings of Desire' meets 'Until The End of The World' (who ever thought they'd come out of a Marvel movie thinking about one Wim Wenders feature, let alone two?)
reviews.author: Bob Chipman

reviews.text: Eternals may be more elegant, with a more creative use of digital effects than its predecessors, but its unjustifiable 157 minutes lack tension, humor and action. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Diego Batlle

reviews.text: Eternals is a nice ride. Chloé Zhao does a strong job of bringing these characters into the spotlight, making us care about them, and leading us into what comes next.
reviews.author: Sherin Nicole

reviews.text: Although the experiment of combining commercial cinema with an indie sensibility doesn't always work, there's a lot worth watching. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Ruben Peralta Rigaud

reviews.text: Oscar-winning filmmaker Chloé Zhao is a gifted director, but this crowded, overly expository Marvel entry doesn't quite come together, despite impressive visuals and an excellent, diverse cast.
reviews.author: Sandie Angulo Chen

reviews.text: The first genuinely bad film from Marvel Films, Chloe Zhao's "Eternals" is a colossal bore, a bloated, meandering super-hero odyssey.
reviews.author: Charles Koplinski

reviews.text: There's a good 90-minute movie buried someplace within these two and a half hours. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Jorge Rivera Rubio

reviews.text: Eternals shoots for the stars, and if the finished feature isn't quite out of this world, it's still close enough to getting there that my interest in seeing where these characters go next is exceedingly high.
reviews.author: Sara Michelle Fetters

reviews.text: "Eternals" istoo much of a not good enough thing.
reviews.author: Adam Graham

reviews.text: Eternals can be heavy-handed and its ambitions arguably exceed its grasp, but at least it's reaching.
reviews.author: Mark Cassidy

reviews.text: Perhaps Eternals will gain traction the more we get to see what the rest of the MCU's Phase 4 involves. On its own, though, the story lacks the excitement that audiences have come to expect from Marvel films.
reviews.author: Alex Bentley

reviews.text: An underwhelming blockbuster that takes itself and its dour characters too seriously.
reviews.author: Jason Gorber

reviews.text: Eternals? Not even close. Though at two hours and 37 minutes it may start to feel like it.
reviews.author: Chris Knight

reviews.text: The film is very prog. But also very pop.
reviews.author: Danny Leigh

reviews.text: This is an ambitious, exciting movie that doesn't entirely stick the landing but remains on par with what we've seen from a successful franchise film.
reviews.author: Jonathan Sim

reviews.text: The whole enterprise remains a supermassive black hole not even a light like Chloé Zhao can escape.
reviews.author: Conor O'Donnell

reviews.text: The story is bloated and underdeveloped, featuring too many characters and a clumsy plot.
reviews.author: Gavia Baker-Whitelaw

reviews.text: Eternals is jammed to the rafters with great ideas, but too many end up weighing the film down instead of letting it fly.
reviews.author: Karen Gordon

reviews.text: This movie is more risk-prone than the majority of Marvel titles. Yet it frustrates, even beyond a screenplay full of self-competing interests. And as far as MCU fatigue goes - well, at this point, it goes pretty far.
reviews.author: Michael Phillips

reviews.text: An overly earnest universe that's short on zippy banter and big on shoddily rendered CGI set-pieces.
reviews.author: Alistair Harkness

reviews.text: A Marvel Cinematic Universe origin story that suffers from all the baggy, convoluted drawbacks of the form.
reviews.author: Ann Hornaday

reviews.text: [Chloé Zhao] is somehow out of her element here as she struggles to juggle multiple character arcs throughout the ponderous 157-minute length.
reviews.author: Casey Chong

reviews.text: There are moments of visual and narrative brilliance, but it's ultimately a film that bites off more than it can chew.
reviews.author: Doug Jamieson

reviews.text: Ms. Zhao has taken on this sprawling storyline which spans over 7000 years...and after 157 minutes, that's exactly what it feels like.
reviews.author: Jeanne Kaplan

reviews.text: Marvel has taken a director of rare sensitivity and forced her into the superhero grinder, where only flecks of her emotionally textured, magic-hour romanticism remain.
reviews.author: Mark Keizer

reviews.text: ...serves as an uncommonly grand and poignant take on superheroes.
reviews.author: Cain Noble-Davies

reviews.text: Its an ambitious, sprawling story that feels bogged down by it's own superhero antics and messy execution. For better or worse, its Marvel's least Marvel film to date. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Fico Cangiano

reviews.text: Eternals suffers from bland lead characters... and the villains are very lackluster.
reviews.author: John Nguyen

reviews.text: Chloé Zhao's choices evoke both the epoch-spanning timeline of the film as well as the planetary change happening to the Earth right now.
reviews.author: Ryan Silberstein

reviews.text: "Eternals" is a strange film, both within context and on its own. But in the lookalike, soundalike and corporately synergistic MCU, perhaps that's not such a bad thing.
reviews.author: Katie Walsh

reviews.text: Zhao is an undeniably gifted filmmaker, but Eternals does not make effective use of those gifts and by the end, there is the undeniable sense that she became as tired of the whole thing while making it as viewers will be while watching it.
reviews.author: Peter Sobczynski

reviews.text: A blockbuster of unusual gentle beauty that also strains to fulfill the gargantuan requirements of a massive action spectacle.
reviews.author: Christy Lemire

reviews.text: Marvel's latest is a litany of cosmic, philosophical and expositional verbiage, clumsily expressed by a talented but uneven cast through their cryptic characters, that try to pass it off as thematic and emotional depth. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Mario Alegre

reviews.text: The franchise's most ambitious outing yet, a beautifully shot epic full of wonder and imagination.
reviews.author: Joey Morona

reviews.text: There's not enough apparent experience with anything approaching human emotions to make an exploration of these beings' complicated feelings possible, much less interesting.
reviews.author: Joshua Starnes

reviews.text: There are so many flickers of fabulous texture and life struggling valiantly to get out, that it makes the general inertia and frustrayting flatness even more painful.
reviews.author: Stefan Kyriazis

reviews.text: The single most unique and visually stunning Marvel movie ever... a return to the Grand Hollywood Epic on the biggest scale possible. While it, understandably, may not work for some, this behemoth of a picture is a hugely welcome and refreshing entry
reviews.author: Dave Lee

reviews.text: Too many characters, too little plot, too many flashbacks, not enough action, and too much conversation.
reviews.author: Grant Watson

reviews.text: One of the least engaging of all the Marvel movies-big and splashy but lumbering and strangely dull.
reviews.author: Frank Swietek

reviews.text: "Eternals" makes history as the most diverse superhero movie in terms of race, gender, orientation, age and abilities...and that's remarkable...But that doesn't change the fact that they're stuck in a story that's dull and predictable.
reviews.author: Cary Darling

reviews.text: It's way too much character development for one movie - just imagine if we had met all of the Avengers at the same time
reviews.author: Alex Hudson

reviews.text: Some rough edges, but we should cherish a glossy blockbuster that has something to say.
reviews.author: David Jenkins

reviews.text: In the end, Eternals is a fine movie - and sometimes significantly more than that - that is too mired in exposition and predictable, franchise-informed plotting.
reviews.author: Tyler Smith

reviews.text: Eternals was always going to be a bit of a weird one... [it's] different, yes, but it's not bad on its own.
reviews.author: Alexis Nedd

reviews.text: Zhao has graduated from delicate artisanal indies to overprocessed, soul-challenged, assembly-line Hollywood junk in record time.
reviews.author: Kyle Smith

reviews.text: Eternals is not a bad movie. It is ambitious and tries hard to be different from the rest. However, it is ultimately unsatisfying in that most of the film is full of promises for other stories to come. Let us hope those promises are not empty ones.
reviews.author: Alan Cerny

reviews.text: "Eternals" isn't a bad movie. It's just not a particularly satisfying one, its scale proving untamable, even for Zhao.
reviews.author: Bill Goodykoontz

reviews.text: A jumble of clunky dialogue and exposition dumps with no stakes until the typical VFX-packed climactic fights. Eternals is one of the most flavorless films in the Marvel Universe.
reviews.author: Matt Lynch

reviews.text: Chloé Zhao presents some of the biggest strengths of Eternals with her direction, but also some of its biggest weaknesses with her writing.
reviews.author: Joey Magidson

reviews.text: Zhao is a baffling choice: a filmmaker who is ill-equipped and out of her element, with her discomfort visible across nearly every frame of the film.
reviews.author: Barry Hertz

reviews.text: Those expecting something on par with her previous film will no doubt be disappointed, but Zhao turns her hand to big budget filmmaking with relative ease.
reviews.author: Emma Simmonds

reviews.text: Eternals is missing all of the ingredients that made that first Avengers work.
reviews.author: Josh Spiegel

reviews.text: Eternals is unlikely to leave audiences wanting more (or remembering much), though it may well whet the appetite for the day when the Fantastic Four and X-Men finally arrive.
reviews.author: Michael Burgin

reviews.text: ...won't sell many toys, subscriptions or tickets for Disney. If nothing else, it'll remind audiences what it feels like to be bored to distraction in the cinema...
reviews.author: Eddie Harrison

reviews.text: I'm sorry to tell you this movie is a mess.
reviews.author: Nell Minow

reviews.text: One of the most humanist MCU movies ever made. It's an exhilarating, suspenseful and visually dazzling spectacle with a surprisingly warm, beating heart. By treating the characters as human beings, Zhao treats the audience as human beings, too.
reviews.author: Avi Offer

reviews.text: Don't blame the progressive nods for film's failures ... the limp plot does the damage.
reviews.author: Christian Toto

reviews.text: Eternals is going to be a divisive movie because it doesn't really work at the end of the day. There is too much exposition, the pacing and structure are a mess, and the story of love in all its forms gets lost.
reviews.author: Kaitlyn Booth

reviews.text: ETERNALS undoubtedly [expands] the universe of possible stories [as] the series looks to move into a new era. However, the conflicting approaches felt here reveal that this range of films isn't ready or willing to expand how it tells those stories.
reviews.author: Jim Ross

reviews.text: Eternals is Marvel's first attempt at making raw drama. The characters have depth, the score & visuals are unmatched, but I wished they'd committed to the genre change more
reviews.author: Samuel Leggett Jr.

reviews.text: The film pushes back against the usual complaints offered up by those who harbor a performative disdain for Marvel's cinematic output.
reviews.author: Glen Weldon

reviews.text: Where Kubrick and Clarke took seriously the idea that human evolution may be prompted by alien intercession, Eternalsmakes the whole thing part of some gargantuan, intergalactic eugenics experiment wrapped in pop-philosophy and popcorn-authoritarianism.
reviews.author: Wade Major

reviews.text: Eternals is deeply emotional and alters the Marvel formula we know, which some will love and some will hate.
reviews.author: Diandra Reviews

reviews.text: It is entertaining and mostly fast-paced - until the interminable bombastic finale that goes on for many minutes longer than it should - and will please the MU fans.
reviews.author: Robin Clifford

reviews.text: Representation should be the headline-grabber for Eternals, but instead, the conversation around the film will likely focus on how much of a disappointment it is.
reviews.author: Bernard Boo

reviews.text: The star-studded supergod origin story is all bland fight sequences, cold flashbacks, and blank faces taking in stunning vistas.
reviews.author: Tirhakah Love

reviews.text: It's the ambiguity, the attention to a person's capacity for contradiction and change, that sets Zhao's MCU debut apart...
reviews.author: Nina Li Coomes

reviews.text: This sounds kind of fun. And I wish it were. But with the exception of Kumail Nanjiani who offers, without question, the only real reason to see the movie, the story takes itself far too seriously for fun or, really, even logic.
reviews.author: Megan Basham

reviews.text: Ultimately, the film feels like a pet between two owners, and it's confused on exactly who to run to.
reviews.author: Murjani Rawls

reviews.text: A particular dud, and Marvel's worst in years. The mythology is ridiculous, the cast overstuffed, and the action unimpressive.
reviews.author: Stephen Silver

reviews.text: Tropes be damned, Zhao carves out unexpectedly human immortals who actually care about each other. They love and hate and fight and forgive and feud and feel together. It's a refreshingly emotional take.
reviews.author: Rosie Knight

reviews.text: This is the first post-Endgame entry that I can happily call a great movie while seeing the franchise finally evolve in maturity and take bold risks in its storytelling.
reviews.author: Rendy Jones

reviews.text: If Eternals stuck to the multi-million dollar blueprint, it could have been one of the more fascinating MCU entries instead of the most disappointing effort to date.
reviews.author: Jeffrey Lyles

reviews.text: Such heady motivations, coupled with heroism, is a lovely core away from the usual costumed good vs. evil throwdowns, but it's very, very profuse, complete with all of the intergalactic gibberish in between.
reviews.author: Don Shanahan

reviews.text: A Marvel epic that values personal connections over spectacle? Sorry adrenaline junkies, but that's what Oscar-winning, indie director Chloe Zhao brings to her first blockbuster. The result is uneven, but memorably inclusive and unique.
reviews.author: Peter Travers

reviews.text: In many ways Eternals is not a Chloe Zhao problem as much as it is an MCU problem. After the lights came back on my first thought was that this is where comic book movies have "jumped the shark".
reviews.author: Leo Brady

reviews.text: Certainly a revamp, even if it doesn't prove to be a particularly refreshing one.
reviews.author: Emily Wheeler

reviews.text: In the end, the movie was reliably entertaining as, generally speaking, the MCU is... [But] the concept of Eternals is a lot more interesting than the execution of Eternals.
reviews.author: Jeremy Jahns

reviews.text: It's ugly, charisma-free, dour, overlong, exposition-heavy, patronizing, and, worst of all, it has none of the heart even feinted at by the least successful films within the MCU canon.
reviews.author: Nick Johnston

reviews.text: it's pretty clear that Zhao's empathy for unaffected performers rambling in lingering magic-hour landscapes has won the day.
reviews.author: Walter Chaw

reviews.text: "Here is a list of things not to do, if you want to make a Marvel movie that will not be mocked until Tony Stark returns to life."
reviews.author: David Poland

reviews.text: The film works on two levels, the cosmic and fantastic, that of the celestials, and the human, the dramatic, but the mixture of the two does not quite come together completely. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Alejandro G. Calvo

reviews.text: For viewers with an interest in theology and the repackaging of same as superhero subtext for the masses - this is compelling stuff. But for those who expect the tightly wound Marvel machine... this isn't that.
reviews.author: Luke Y. Thompson

reviews.text: Marvel's Eternals takes an intriguing turn towards the grown and sexy but doesn't hit the thrilling action heights of peak MCU.
reviews.author: André Hereford

reviews.text: Meant to be Shakespearean in tone but is too often blocked like Shakespeare in the Park.
reviews.author: Matt Oakes

reviews.text: It takes a special kind of movie anti-magic to make an entire audience indifferent to the potential destruction of the planet and the elimination of all life and Earth. "Eternals" manages it.
reviews.author: Mick LaSalle

reviews.text: Zhao, a director whose previous three films have all centered on the everyday lives of working-class rural outsiders, seems ill-suited to a movie of this scale and frankly uninterested in the fight scenes.
reviews.author: Dana Stevens

reviews.text: The most unique of the MCU universe, Eternals adds the largest dimension of new mythology and universe expansion than any film before it.
reviews.author: John Campea

reviews.text: Eternals offers a totally unique Marvel experience saturated in emotion and delivered on a grand, stunning scale.
reviews.author: Caitlin Kennedy

reviews.text: Eternals is almost a miraculous film.
reviews.author: Richard Propes

reviews.text: Watching Chloé Zhao's The Rider made me want to learn horseback riding. Nomadland illustrated the reality houseless Americans face and offered a window into the American West. Both intertwine fiction and reality. I knew Eternals was going to be different.
reviews.author: Patricia Puentes

reviews.text: While Eternals may be Chloé Zhao's most conventional effort and falls prey to the typical faults of the franchise, she manages to elevate the blockbuster formula to craft one of Marvel's best films yet.
reviews.author: Diego Andaluz

reviews.text: Marvel has its first existential crisis, coming to terms with not only what it means to be a hero but also what it means to be a God. It's extremely ambitious, and while it doesn't completely soar, it still opens a whole new realm of possibilities.
reviews.author: Rohan Patel

reviews.text: Involves a lot of windy locations, sparse imagination for action, and a cast of characters who are seldom interesting.
reviews.author: Brian Orndorf

reviews.text: While I can respect that the MCU took a risk by telling an ambitious and different kind of story, the story and storytelling simply didn't match the film's ambitions.
reviews.author: Sean Chandler

reviews.text: People will decide for themselves whether its innovations are enough or not, but for me it was somewhat disappointing. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Mikel Zorrilla

reviews.text: From visuals to music choice, there's a lack of style here that is only further emphasized by the film's refusal to focus.
reviews.author: Cassie da Costa

reviews.text: Zhao's imprint can even be felt in special effects featuring celestial shapes, natural stone and double decker buses turned into a shower of rose petals.
reviews.author: Laura Clifford

reviews.text: It's a different kind of superhero movie; not to everyone's taste, but made for us all.
reviews.author: Moira MacDonald

reviews.text: Eternals is so busy showing off what it can do, where it can go, that it bypasses and overlooks what it really has to offer. There are real dilemmas, real battles of interest buried beneath the soft-pedaled, naturally-lit, cozy surfaces of this movie.
reviews.author: K. Austin Collins

reviews.text: While I appreciate that Eternals takes a creative risk with its time-jumping events, its convoluted plot ultimately lets it down.
reviews.author: Mike Sorrentino

reviews.text: Eternals feels like a balloon that tried to hold it all together but was filled to bursting; it's too much-and not enough. The result is a very ambitious, very well made, kind of flat, and unfortunately forgettable film.
reviews.author: Germain Lussier

reviews.text: It flies high, grapples with huge themes and ideas, tries to keep check with humour and heart, but the whole thing feels so overblown and overwrought that you kind of walk out of the screen in a daze.
reviews.author: Brian Lloyd

reviews.text: This film is achingly earnest in tackling issues of diversity and representation, but fails as engrossing entertainment
reviews.author: Jana Monji

reviews.text: A film that is constantly at war with itself, for nearly three hours.
reviews.author: Kyle Pinion

reviews.text: What seemed like the perfect marriage of filmmaker and studio, Oscar winner Chloé Zhao and Marvel Studios, turns out to be one of, if not, the biggest misfires since the Marvel Cinematic Universe began.
reviews.author: Nate Adams

reviews.text: Although the dramatic shift in tone from the rest of the universe may be difficult for some to swallow, The Eternals is a much bigger accomplishment in filmmaking than your average Marvel movie.
reviews.author: Joe Passmore

reviews.text: Eternals offers a bold yet epic vision that further reinforces a new creative direction in the franchise.
reviews.author: Katie Smith-Wong

reviews.text: Its main downfall is a confusing script with inconsistently written characters stuck in a timeline that makes it impossible to build momentum or tell a story that makes sense.
reviews.author: Rachel Wagner

reviews.text: Despite the depth of the ensemble (and the acting talents assembled to bring it to life), these Eternals really only come in three varieties: brooding, quippy, and both.
reviews.author: A.A. Dowd

reviews.text: Zhao's Eternals may just set a precedent that could revitalize the MCU moving forward by leaning on its adult themes and new opportunities. This won't be for everyone, that's for sure. But it's exciting nonetheless.
reviews.author: Douglas Davidson

reviews.text: The Marvel Cinematic Universe wades chin deep into a soap opera river of melodramatic tears. Director Chloé Zhao treads sappy with a convoluted exploration of relationships in Eternals.
reviews.author: Julian Roman

reviews.text: This film is massive on every level, both with its story and scale. At times, the narrative can come across as a bit messy, but its heart always shines through. Zhao has crafted something so different from the rest of the MCU.
reviews.author: Austin Burke

reviews.text: For a film about millennia-old space gods with X-Men powers... Eternals feels decidedly pedestrian, its flashes of naturalism still drowned in the usual Feige trappings.
reviews.author: Clint Worthington

reviews.text: Marvel films go down easy for me, but none of them -- none of them -- wear well on repeated viewing.
reviews.author: Kenneth R. Morefield

reviews.text: Thank the cine-gods that Chloé Zhao was able to take all those innocuous prerequisites and create a film that is gorgeously photographed and focuses on the intimate moments between the characters allowing them to breathe.
reviews.author: Frank J. Avella

reviews.text: At once bloated and rushed, Eternals suffers from frequent lurches in tempo that dispel its occasional moments of tranquil thoughtfulness.
reviews.author: Jake Cole

reviews.text: Marvel's Eternals boasts a keen directing eye, with beautiful shots throughout, but an inconsistent tone and one-dimensional themes prevent it from being among Marvel's best.
reviews.author: Sheraz Farooqi

reviews.text: Zhao's imprint is... hard to miss in the movie's steady thrum of melancholy and its deeper, odder character arcs.
reviews.author: Leah Greenblatt

reviews.text: A visually stunning film, Eternals blows the doors off of Cosmic Marvel, creates its own path in the cinematic universe...
reviews.author: Kate Sánchez

reviews.text: At times Zhao's superhero epic is able to breakaway from the Marvel mold, but in the end the movie is still beholden to the broader MCU.
reviews.author: Sean Mulvihill

reviews.text: While the film is bogged down in exposition, Chloé Zhao delivers a very meaningful superhero Marvel film that ponders the question of whether the human race is worth saving. This MCU entry has an indie spirit but delivers great action too.
reviews.author: Lupe Rodriguez Haas

reviews.text: The things that made Chloe Zhao's indie movies special didn't translate to massive blockbuster filmmaking.
reviews.author: Matt Singer

reviews.text: Zhao manages to find the right mix of humanity and science fiction in Eternals while taking audiences on an adventure.
reviews.author: Danielle Solzman

reviews.text: Marvel was the last studio I'd have expected to tell a story about Angels questioning their God. Though it doesn't always achieve its ambitions, it is easily the studio's most interesting film in years.
reviews.author: Evan Dossey

reviews.text: Seriously, what a snooze. Fresh off of winning the Best Director Oscar for "Nomadland," Chloé Zhao has upchucked one of the MCU's worst movies in ages.
reviews.author: Johnny Oleksinski

reviews.text: Eternals has the expected thrilling action scenes but the non-action scenes might be too quiet and introspective for some fans ... However, the showdowns in the last third of the movie make up for the meandering story in the rest of Eternals.
reviews.author: Carla Hay

reviews.text: This big budget action film will hit theaters just in time for Thanksgiving, which reaches the chef's kiss of utter perfection because it's a $200 million turkey.
reviews.author: Louisa Moore

reviews.text: It doesn't always work, but it is undeniably the most ambitious Marvel movie (and it didn't need 25 other movies as stepping stones to a colossal-length grand finale), pitting religious and familial duties against one another
reviews.author: Robert Kojder

reviews.text: There's a small comfort in knowing that there probably never will be a Marvel film like this one. Even if you end up hating it or finding it completely forgettable.
reviews.author: Jon Negroni

reviews.text: A frustratingly protracted rumpus of showdowns and duels in which characters spontaneously summon unknown talents to best combatants with equally undisclosed faculties.
reviews.author: Mike Massie

reviews.text: The future of Marvel is cosmic perfection. Even at its most spacey, the film never forgets its very human soul.
reviews.author: EJ Moreno

reviews.text: The film speaks to what it means to be pawns in someone else's game and be forced to find reasons to continue. Each character seems passionate about moving forward without the reigns of their Celestial creator.
reviews.author: Danielle Broadway

reviews.text: The Eternals experience life on Earth across thousands of years, and with the help of a strong ensemble cast, Zhao tracks their shared awe and despair as observers of history.
reviews.author: Shirley Li

reviews.text: Worth seeing just to experience the bizarre narrative corners IP-driven filmmaking and mindless synergy have painted these filmmakers into.
reviews.author: Vincent Mancini

reviews.text: Eternals is well-constructed and thought out... [However] Chloé Zhao demonstrates with her first blockbuster how quickly something resembling a "style" can be swallowed up by an agent as voracious as Marvel. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Alberto Corona

reviews.text: Eternals is Marvel's Suicide Squad... but with a slightly better ending.
reviews.author: Edward Douglas

reviews.text: Feels a bit like homework: If you don't want the rest of the class to move on without you, it's mandatory; but in the end, you'll just be glad to turn it in and move along to the next thing.
reviews.author: Larry Carroll

reviews.text: The scale of Eternals is unlike anything we've seen to date in the MCU, but it also ends up in a movie that just has too much on its plate.
reviews.author: Ian Sandwell

reviews.text: A disappointment of cosmic proportions, Eternals never takes off due to a pedestrian script that wastes a galaxy of talent. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Nestor Bentancor

reviews.text: The fight-driven action is fun - Jolie really has a ball - but it all feels geared towards setting up further adventures.
reviews.author: James Mottram

reviews.text: A convoluted cosmic misfire and one of Marvel's dullest efforts in years.
reviews.author: Rodrigo Perez

reviews.text: Eternals is a decent flick, but it rarely manages to rise above what we've already seen from the MCU.
reviews.author: JimmyO

reviews.text: Eternals will likely be one of the more divisive films in the Marvel Cinematic Universe. No matter how you feel about Eternals, there's no denying Phase Four is off to an exciting start.
reviews.author: Jamie Jirak

reviews.text: Eternals is beautiful in its visuals and its storytelling.
reviews.author: Josephine L.

reviews.text: The weight of complicated exposition weakens the energy of Eternals a little too often. It's at its best when the focus is on the Eternals recreating their family -- the humor of it and the passion when they fight for each other and the things they love.
reviews.author: Perri Nemiroff

reviews.text: Eternals itself is far from perfect, but it does indicate that the Marvel movie factory is not content to rest on its already massive bed of laurels.
reviews.author: Don Kaye

reviews.text: There are enough good elements here to warrant a fresh tomato, but wow did Chloe Zhao not understand the MCU assignment. Madden, Jolie, Nanjiani & Ridloff are the standouts.
reviews.author: Grace Randolph

reviews.text: Visually stunning. Marvel's most ambitious film to date. Leans a bit heavier on the exposition. The most different film in the entire MCU which is refreshing.
reviews.author: Wendy Lee Szany

reviews.text: Eternals may not be the worst of Marvel's movies, but it's undoubtedly the most disappointing.
reviews.author: Nicholas Barber

reviews.text: Boy, does this patchy, paceless film go on for an eternity.
reviews.author: Dulcie Pearce

reviews.text: It's constantly engaged in a kind of grit-toothed authenticity theatre, going out of its way to show you it's doing all the things proper cinema does, even though none of them bring any discernible benefit whatsoever to the film at hand.
reviews.author: Robbie Collin

reviews.text: Zhao seamlessly uses expert filmmaking skills weaned on a smaller scale to great effect on this HUGE canvas.
reviews.author: Pete Hammond

reviews.text: The most emotionally intimate Marvel story to date...
reviews.author: Damon Smith

reviews.text: 'Eternals' shows Marvel making the same mistakes (generic superhero characters, dull effects-driven action, making the entire film a prologue for the sequel, etc.) as its rivals.
reviews.author: Scott Mendelson

reviews.text: You walk out in the depressing realization that you've just seen one of the more interesting movies Marvel will ever make, and hopefully the least interesting one Chloé Zhao will ever make.
reviews.author: Justin Chang

reviews.text: One of Marvel's most ambitious movies in years is also one of its weakest since "Thor: The Dark World."
reviews.author: Kirsten Acuna

reviews.text: This is a film that asks on a grand scale questions we grapple with every day. How do we navigate and understand difference? Why do we value humanity so much when humans often do not seem to value each other?
reviews.author: Oliver Jones

reviews.text: With characters and concepts this strong, Zhao's quite right to take her time.
reviews.author: Charlotte O'Sullivan

reviews.text: Eternals isn't bad at all and ranks among the better entries of the MCU.
reviews.author: Brandon Zachary

reviews.text: It's not exactly boring - there's always something new to behold - but nor it is particularly exciting, and it lacks the breezy wit of Marvel's best movies.
reviews.author: Steve Rose

reviews.text: Chloé Zhao's intimate style gives the movie a more mature feel, but it doesn't affect the story enough to make it "a different Marvel movie". [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Jesus Agudo

reviews.text: While not without messiness and over-plotting that bogs down and overcomplicates the narrative, Eternals succeeds as a vast and unrepentantly serious bit of world building with a moral quandary at its center.
reviews.author: Esther Zuckerman

reviews.text: The depth of feeling helps counter the choppy storytelling in this new tangent in the MCU narrative.
reviews.author: David Rooney

reviews.text: Zhao delivers a uniquely evocative, extraordinarily epic superhero film that features a thought-provoking, thematically dense narrative and enriching emotional stakes.
reviews.author: Courtney Howard

reviews.text: Eternals certainly doesn't lack for ambition, but for now, Marvel -- emboldened by its success -- has reached for the stars without quite getting there.
reviews.author: Brian Lowry

reviews.text: Utilizing Zhao's penchant for naturalistic environments, Eternals looks unlike any other Marvel movie and isperhapsthe most welcoming for MCU neophytes in forever.
reviews.author: Brian Truitt

reviews.text: Eternals is visually elegant thanks to Zhao's creative sensibilities, but such a narrative undertaking does get the better of the filmmaker more than a handful of instances.
reviews.author: Matt Donato

reviews.text: Eternals is a mess.
reviews.author: Joshua Rivera

reviews.text: Can't these movies do anything else? Is it too much to ask the most dominant kind of cinema on the planet to shake things up and challenge itself in a more significant way?
reviews.author: David Ehrlich

reviews.text: [Zhao is] a master craftswoman, and "Eternals," while too long (157 minutes? really?), is a squarely fun and gratifying watch.
reviews.author: Owen Gleiberman

reviews.text: A mishmash of well-meaning, yet jarringly verbose and bafflingly incoherent nonsense which is only just about saved by some half decent performances.
reviews.author: Linda Marric

reviews.text: After so many Marvel movies that give lip service to the thornier ramifications of its hero narratives, there's an earnestness to the operatic stakes in "Eternals" that somehow helps fuse what's physically spectacular and philosophical about it.
reviews.author: Robert Abele

reviews.text: Chloé Zhao gives the MCU just the kick in the pants it needs at this phase in its evolution.
reviews.author: Neil Smith

reviews.text: It's impressive and mythic and wild and dazzling, yet it also feels strangely diluted.
reviews.author: Hoai-Tran Bui

reviews.text: Eternals is beautifully shot and terrifically acted, but it bites off more than it can chew in its third act.
reviews.author: Amelia Emberwing

reviews.text: Director Chlo Zhao's entry into the superhero world is assured, ambitious and told on a dizzyingly cosmic scale- but even it can't escape the clichs of superhero storytelling.
reviews.author: John Nugent

reviews.text: While Eternals has most of the benchmarks of a Marvel movie, Zhao's sprawling superhero epic is unlike anything the MCU has produced before.
reviews.author: Molly Freeman

reviews.text: Unlike anything ever seen in the MCU before. The story is dense but allowed to breathe. Visually stunning, epic action & emotional story. A perfect introduction to new heroes.
reviews.author: Tessa Smith

reviews.text: Setting aside whatever faults I found, Eternals is decidedly different and more conceptually interesting than most MCU entries.
reviews.author: Aaron Neuwirth

synopsis: Marvel Studios' Eternals features an exciting new team of Super Heroes in the Marvel Cinematic Universe, ancient aliens who have been living on Earth in secret for thousands of years. Following the events of Avengers: Endgame, an unexpected tragedy forces them out of the shadows to reunite against mankind's most ancient enemy, the Deviants.
